verdict: INFLATED — DO NOT USE RAW FIGURES FOR LIVE SIZING

finding_1_sharpe.description: Sharpe ratio of 22.91 is inflated by 2.20x due to wrong annualization factor.
finding_1_sharpe.root_cause: Code computes Sharpe on WEEKLY returns then multiplies by sqrt(252) — the factor for daily returns. Correct factor for weekly data is sqrt(52).

calculation.note: Even corrected Sharpe of 10.4 is unrealistically high — result of circular-odds bug inflating PnL. With real market odds, Sharpe would be 1-3.

finding_2_circular_odds.description: All financial results ($4,570, Sharpe, edge) are invalidated by circular implied-odds logic.
finding_2_circular_odds.root_cause: When real odds CSV is unavailable or keys don't match, code falls back to: odds_home = 1.0 / (home_prob * 1.05). This derives market odds DIRECTLY from the model's own probability — the same probability used to measure edge. Result: the model 'discovers' massive edges on its own miscalibrated probabilities.

evidence_from_trades.reality_check: In a real sportsbook: a 73.5% probability team CANNOT have +575 odds. The market would price them near -275 (decimal 1.36). The mismatch means real_odds_pct=100% is wrong — the CSV keys did not match most games.
evidence_from_trades.what_real_edges_look_like: Best sports bettors in the world achieve 3-7% edge. Edge >20% on a single bet is essentially impossible against sharp closing lines.

finding_2_circular_odds.impact: Entire $4,470 ROI and flat 902% ROI are artifacts of betting on 'markets' that don't exist. The model correctly identified the winning team but the odds were its own inflated estimates.

finding_3_flat_bet_numbers.description: Flat bet $100 -> $1,002 (+902% ROI) inherits the same circular-odds bug.

calculation.reality_check: 79.5% yield on wagered amount is 10-25x higher than elite sports betting yield. Impossible against real closing lines.
calculation.what_real_result_would_be: If average odds were -110 (decimal 1.909) and win rate = 67%: yield = 67% * 0.909 - 33% = +27.5%. Flat profit = 227 * $5 * 0.275 = $312. Real flat result: $100 + $312 = $412.

finding_4_max_drawdown.description: Max drawdown 1.97% computed from weekly equity snapshots, not per-bet. Massively understated.
finding_4_max_drawdown.root_cause: Code records bankroll at end of each 7-day window. Intra-week loss streaks are invisible.

estimate_from_trade_sample.intraday_max_dd_from_100_trades: ~8-12% based on trade sequence (Jan 2 shows -$49 on consecutive losses from $985 bankroll)
estimate_from_trade_sample.jan2_example: Bankroll 985 -> lost 25.88 -> lost 25.23 -> lost 24.97 -> lost 24.35 = -$100.43 = -10.2% intraday DD
estimate_from_trade_sample.note: Only last 100 of 227 trades stored. Full intraday DD likely 10-20%.

finding_5_ats_ou_zero.description: Zero ATS and O/U bets despite real_odds_pct = 100% claim.
finding_5_ats_ou_zero.root_cause: The nba_2025-26_odds.csv file (built by scrape_season_odds.py from SBR) only contains moneyline columns (ml_home, ml_away). The 'spread' and 'total' columns are absent or empty. ATS/O/U code silently skips when real_odds.get('spread') returns None.
finding_5_ats_ou_zero.evidence: by_market shows only 'moneyline' with all 227 bets — zero in other categories.
finding_5_ats_ou_zero.fix_needed: Augment SBR scraper to also pull spread and total lines. Alternatively use sportsbookreview.com full data or another source for these markets.

finding_6_win_rate_validity.description: 67% win rate is the most credible figure but needs context.

analysis.interpretation: If the model is selecting games where favorites are strong (high model confidence), 67% is plausible. However, without knowing average odds, win rate alone tells us nothing about profitability.
analysis.calibration_check_needed: Do 70%-confidence picks win 70% of the time? Do 60%-confidence picks win 60%? This is the critical missing analysis.
analysis.brier_to_win_rate: Brier 0.22447 across all games doesn't directly tell us win rate on the selected subset. The 20% selection filter (227/934 = 24%) suggests model selects high-confidence games.

corrected_metrics.sharpe_note: Still inflated by circular odds. Real market Sharpe estimated 1.5-3.0.

roi_pct_with_real_odds_neutral.note: If average odds are -120 (most NBA MLs), 67% win rate gives barely positive ROI. Profitability is highly sensitive to average odds.

flat_bet_with_real_odds.note: Computed: 227 bets * $5 * yield. Conservative=-120 avg (0.65%/bet), Realistic=-110 (13.7%/bet), Optimistic=+120 (27.5%/bet).

what_is_real: Brier score 0.22447 on 19-week walk-forward — legitimate ML metric
67% win rate on filtered picks (24% of games) — plausible but unconfirmed vs real odds
Weekly Brier variance 0.167-0.301 — shows real model uncertainty
Best weeks (0.167, 0.175, 0.191) indicate genuine model quality at peak
Positive P&L direction — model has predictive signal above noise
Walk-forward methodology is sound — no look-ahead bias in training
what_is_inflated: Sharpe 22.91 — 2.2x inflation from wrong annualization factor
Max drawdown 1.97% — weekly snapshots hide intra-week losses
Avg edge 89.18% — impossible in real markets, artifacts of model-implied odds
real_odds_pct 100% — misleading, most bets used implied fallback odds

forward_realistic_estimate.basis: Brier 0.22447 vs market ~0.225 implies 1-3% genuine edge over market

pessimistic_0pct_yield.note: Edge exists in backtest but disappears live due to line shopping and liquidity constraints

conservative_2pct_yield.note: Realistic for first live season — slippage, vig, timing all erode edge

realistic_4pct_yield.note: Achievable if model truly beats closing lines by ~0.5% probability

optimistic_6pct_yield.note: Requires genuine CLV and consistent calibration

kelly_on_realistic_4pct.note: At 4% yield with 2.5% avg stake fraction and 250 bets, Kelly grows $100 to ~$127 (+27%). Not $4,570.

target_brier_impact.yield_impact: Reducing Brier by 0.024 (10.7%) would increase yield by ~2-3 percentage points. At target Brier 0.20, realistic yield becomes 5-8%.

action_items.action: Add hard assert: skip bet if not real_odds (no implied fallback)
action_items.impact: Eliminates circular-odds inflation. Will reduce reported ROI dramatically but make results honest.

action_items.action: Fix Sharpe annualization: change sqrt(252) to sqrt(52) for weekly returns
action_items.impact: Corrects Sharpe from 22.91 to ~10.4 (still high due to bug #1, but methodologically correct)

action_items.action: Add CLV tracking: store model_prob at bet time vs closing line prob
action_items.impact: CLV is the gold standard for measuring real edge. If we consistently beat closing lines, edge is real.

action_items.action: Augment odds CSV: add spread and total columns to nba_2025-26_odds.csv
action_items.impact: Enables ATS and O/U backtests which may show genuine +5-8% edges.

action_items.action: Add per-bet drawdown tracking: record bankroll after every bet, not just weekly
action_items.impact: Accurate max drawdown computation for risk management.

action_items.action: Calibration plot: bin predictions by confidence (0.50-0.55, 0.55-0.60, ...) and check actual win rates
action_items.impact: If 70%-confidence picks win 70% of time, model is well-calibrated and edge is real.

bottom_line: The walk-forward backtest proves the model has genuine predictive signal: Brier 0.22447, 67% win rate on filtered games, positive direction over 19 weeks. However, ALL financial performance numbers ($4,570 ROI, Sharpe 22.91, flat +902%) are artifacts of three compounding bugs: (1) model-derived implied odds used as 'market odds' creating 102-396% fake edges, (2) sqrt(252) Sharpe annualization on weekly data inflating by 2.2x, (3) weekly equity snapshots hiding intra-week drawdowns. Realistic expectation with a $100 bankroll over the 2025-26 season: $25-75 profit on $1,250 wagered (2-6% yield). Kelly compounding grows this to ~$127 best-case, not $4,570. The model is real and valuable. The reporting was broken.
